## My Thinking

I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over 30 years. My father farmed it before me. I know what works here.

This is the Hebei Plain. The soil is good loam. We get rain mostly in summer — not enough for wheat without pumping from the well. Everyone around me does winter wheat followed by summer maize. That's the rotation. It makes sense: wheat goes in October, comes out June. Maize goes right back in, comes out September. Two harvests a year from the same field.

I have about 10 mu. That's what my family works. At my age, I'm not looking to expand. My son helps during harvest but he has a factory job in Xingtai now most of the year.

For wheat, I use the improved variety — something like Shimai 15 or Hengguan. Not the old landrace seeds my grandfather used, but not the fancy new stuff either. It yields steady. I put down base fertilizer before plowing — compound fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium, then urea again at jointing. I irrigate three times: before winter sets in, at jointing in April, and at heading. Rotary till after the maize stover. Two sprays — herbicide in winter, then fungicide and aphid spray in May.

For maize, I plant straight into the wheat stubble with no tilling. Less work, keeps moisture.郑单958 hybrid — everyone uses it, you can get the seed at the co-op. Summer rains handle most of the water. I only pump once if August turns dry. One herbicide spray early, one spray for corn borer and leaf disease later.

I don't try vegetables or anything unusual. At 58, I want reliable. Wheat and maize pay the bills and keep the granary full.
